text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Vytautas Landsbergis was elected the chairman of Lithuania's new parliament on Monday.

- Vilnius police officials have detained a 30-year-old defence attorney suspected of attempting to bribe a prosecutor. It is the first time in Lithuania a defence attorney has been detained. The attorney is known for providing her services to high ranking personalities in Vilnius' criminal world.
- Five people were killed in a car crash on the Panevezys-Kedainiai road on Sunday night.
- The newly founded Property Bank with 83 million litas share capital officially opened on Monday. PB will take over about 800 million litas of bad loans from four problem banks.

- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas intends this week to analyse and provide further suggestions on the draft law from the National Investigation Bureau. The NBI draft law is to be submitted for parliament approval this year.
- The National-Socialist party was founded in Siauliai on Sunday to pursue rightwing ideas in politics and leftwing ideas in economy.
- Siemens Nixdorf Informaatiojarjestelmat won an international tender worth 40-50 million litas to install a state border control information system.
- The biggest beer brewery in Lithuania, Utenos Gerimai, held preliminary negotiations with representatives of Carlsberg last week. The results of the talks are expected to be known in January.
- The share capital of all the commercial banks was nearly two times higher at the end of November at 717.6 million litas compared to early January when it was 376 million litas.
